L5:

L35: ## Frequently asked questions
L36: 
L37: 【7†Image: ASU alumni at Industrious in Tempe】
L38: 
L39: Can I get financial aid?
L40: ASU Universal Learner Courses aren’t eligible for federal financial aid, but you can register for a course for just $25. Once you’ve successfully completed the course, you can convert it to real ASU credits on an official ASU transcript for $400 and you have up to one year to decide if you want to add the credits.
L41: While these courses are not eligible for traditional federal financial aid, 【8†Universal Learner Course fees may qualify as a 529 expense】 depending on your state.
L42: Can I use my employer’s “tuition reimbursement” towards Universal Learner Courses?
L43: 
L44: It depends on the employer. Some learners have successfully gotten their credits reimbursed by their company, so it won’t hurt to ask! It’s always best to talk with your HR department before you attempt to get credit, and be sure to mention this is real college credit provided by Arizona State University.
L45: 
L46: Are these real college courses?
L47: Yes, ASU Universal Learner Courses are university courses taught by the same prestigious faculty and instructors who teach on Arizona State University campuses teach our courses, so the rigor and quality of course materials is the same. The difference? Universal Learner Courses give you the chance to dip your toes into the real college course experience without risk to your wallet or your GPA.
L48: Students receive a transcript after passing and paying for the course that can be used to apply to ASU or transferred to another college. These courses appear identically to a course you would take online or on campus as an enrolled ASU student.

L4: # Frequently asked questions
L5: 
L6: Find answers to common questions about ASU’s flexible pathways to college, designed to make higher education accessible and convenient for all learners.
L7: 
L8: 【2†Image: ASU students sitting near palm trees】
L9: ## About
L10: 
L11: What are ASU Universal Learner Courses?
L12: 
L13: Arizona State University offers an expanding list of open-access courses taught by ASU faculty and available for people who are not formally admitted or enrolled at ASU. Universal Learner Courses (or ULCs) often satisfy general studies requirements or are common prerequisites across a variety of majors.
L14: 
L15: Is this the same course I would take on campus?
L16: Yes, Universal Learner Courses provide a course experience that serves diverse learner audiences and features active learning and project-based assessment. These courses are evaluated and designed by ASU faculty to align with the same courses on campus and feature the same faculty.
L17: 
L18: 【3†Image: Paper plane graphic】
L19: ## Registration
L20: 
L21: How do I register?
L22: 
L23: You can register at 【4†ulc.asu.edu】 by clicking on the “Register” button.
L24: 
L25: Do I have to apply to ASU?
L26: 
L27: No, anyone who is not enrolled at ASU can take Universal Learner Courses.
L28: However, if you are planning to pursue a degree at ASU, you must 【5†submit an application†asuonline.asu.edu】 and we highly recommend that you do that as soon as possible so that your transition into ASU upon completion of the program is a seamless experience and we can better support you.
L29: Can current ASU students take these courses?
L30: Admitted, degree-seeking ASU students cannot take ULCs as they are designed for learners who are not yet enrolled at ASU. Included in the tuition are student support services specifically designed to help currently enrolled students persist toward their goal of graduation. If you are an admitted ASU student, please refer to the 【6†ASU Course Catalog†catalog.apps.asu.edu】 for available courses.
L31: An ASU student may become eligible to enroll in ULCs again if they defer their enrollment, or pass the seven term minimum since an active ASU enrollment. The same rules for disqualified ASU students apply to ULC also, so students who are academically disqualified cannot add ULCs to their ASU transcript.
L32: How old do you have to be to take these courses?
L33: 
L34: There are no age restrictions for Universal Learner Courses. However, these are college-level courses and do require identity verification.
L35: 
L36: How do I verify my identity?
L37: ULC learners are required to authenticate their identity before their course begins with a live photo and an approved form of photo identification. This includes government-issued IDs, school IDs, or birth certificates for learners under 18. Your photo ID must match the name associated with your ASU account.
L38: If you’re under the age of 18, you may provide a birth certificate to begin the course, but if your course requires proctoring, a government-issued ID is required to take the exam and complete the course.
L39: Can I get an ASU ID card after I register?
L40: 
L41: No, ASU ID cards are issued to admitted ASU students only.
L42: 
L43: Will I get an asu.edu email after I register for Universal Learner Courses?
L44: 
L45: No, ASU has transitioned away from issuing emails and supports using personal emails. ASU emails are only issued when a course requires it for the completion of the course. Most courses do not require ASU emails for completion. Learners will not retain access to ASU Gmail once they are no longer actively enrolled in ULCs.
L46: 【7†Image: Person in front of whiteboard graphic】
L47: ## Courses
L48: 
L49: When do I need to be online for my courses?
L50: 
L51: Universal Learner Courses are asynchronous which means they do not have any live content. While there are weekly due dates in most courses, you can complete the coursework when it is convenient for you. Some courses hold live office hours with instructors, but these are not required and the content is recorded and posted in the course to view whenever works best for you.
L52: 
L53: Do I need to order any textbooks or materials?
L54: No, you do not need to order any textbooks or materials. All materials are provided when the course opens.
L55: 
L56: How can I get academic support in my courses?
L57: 
L58: Visit the 【8†ULC Online Study Hub†tutoring.asu.edu】 for academic support. You will need to use your ASURITE to access.
L59: 
L60: How do I access my ASU Gmail account?
L61: ASU emails are only issued when a course requires it for the completion of the course. Most courses do not require ASU emails for completion. Sign in to your 【9†My ASU†my.asu.edu】 and select the Gmail shortcut link located in your shortcuts list. If you don’t see the Gmail shortcut link select View More and select Gmail from the drop-down. You can also access your ASU Gmail by going to 【10†email.asu.edu†email.asu.edu】. If you are unable to access your Gmail, please contact 【11†[email protected]】.
L62: If I unenroll, will it appear on my transcript?
L63: 
L64: No. There is no risk to your academic record with Universal Learner Courses since you don’t pay to add them to your transcript until you choose. If you find that now’s not the time for you to take a course, you can easily unenroll at any time on your learner dashboard.
L65: 
L66: What does on-demand and session-based mean?
L67: On-demand is a course you can start today that can be completed at your own pace. You must spend a minimum of 6 weeks enrolled in the course and have 1 year to complete it. Session-based is a course with a specific start date and the structure of a cohort with other learners and due dates.
L68: 
L69: Is on-demand or session-based right for me?
L70: Not all courses are available in both formats but we encourage learners to enroll in session-based courses whenever possible. We find that learners are more successful in session-based courses where they can move through the course material with other learners and have due dates for assignments. On-demand courses are best for learners who have to take long absences from internet connectivity or high school students that use these courses for dual enrollment.
L71: 
L72: How long do I have access to the course?
L73: You’ll have access to the course materials (readings, videos, presentations, etc.) for 2 weeks after the course ends for all session-based courses and on-demand courses will be closed upon request for academic credit.
L74: 
L75: How can I get enrollment verification?
L76: A letter can be written verifying your enrollment in your current Universal Learner Courses. To request a letter, please reach out to our support team at 【12†[email protected]】. This letter can only be sent directly to the learner and cannot be provided to other institutions or organizations.
L77: 
L78: Can I get my student loans deferred while taking Universal Learner Courses?
L79: No, we are unable to complete any loan-related forms. Learners enrolled in Universal Learner Courses are not considered admitted to Arizona State University. At this time, the only documentation we are able to provide is an Enrollment Verification (EV) letter.
L80: 
L81: 【13†Image: Medal graphic】
L82: ## Payment
L83: 
L84: How much are Universal Learner Courses?
L85: 
L86: You’ll pay a $25 course enrollment fee to reserve your place in the course. If you’d like to add the course to your ASU transcript for college credit, you’ll need to pay a fee of $400 following the completion of your course if you are satisfied with your grade.
L87: 
L88: Are there any hidden fees?
L89: No, we only have two fees associated with our courses:
L90: • $25 course enrollment fee
L91: • $400 to add it to your ASU transcript for college credit (This fee is paid at the end of the course if you are satisfied with your grade.)
L92: 
L93: Can I get financial aid?
L94: Although Universal Learner Courses aren’t eligible for federal financial aid, you can register for just $25 per course. This low cost makes higher education accessible without loans or debt. After passing your course, you have up to one year to add the credits to your ASU transcript for $400 per course.
L95: 
L96: Should I complete a FAFSA?
L97: If you are using Universal Learner Courses to earn admission to ASU, yes. We recommend completing a FAFSA when you are nearing the end of your Earned Admission courses, before you are admitted to ASU. Learn more about submitting your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) 【14†here†asuonline.asu.edu】.
L98: 
L99: I enrolled in a course that I am no longer interested in taking. Can I get a refund?
L100: You may unenroll from ULCs at any time without impacting your academic record. If you unenroll within 10 calendar days of the course start date, you will automatically be issued a refund of the $25 enrollment fee. You may only receive one automatic refund per course. If you need to unenroll from a course a second time, please contact support at 【11†[email protected]】. Refunds will not be issued for the purchase of ASU credit.
L101: 
L102: Are these courses covered by military benefits?
L103: These courses are not currently covered by any military benefit.
L104: 
L105: Where can I get a 1098-T tax form?
L106: 
L107: You may request a 1098-T from Student Business Services via email at 【11†[email protected]】 or phone at 1(855)278-5080. ULC learners cannot access 1098-T information from their 【15†My ASU†my.asu.edu】 page.
L108: 
L109: Can I use my employer’s “tuition reimbursement” toward Universal Learner Courses?
L110: It depends on the employer. Some ULC participants have successfully gotten their credits reimbursed by their company, so it won’t hurt to ask! It’s always best to talk with your HR department before you attempt to convert, and be sure to mention this is real college credit provided by Arizona State University.
L111: 
L112: 【16†Image: Building with columns graphic】
L113: ## College credit
L114: 
L115: How do these courses appear on my transcript?
L116: 
L117: These courses appear identically to a course you would take online or on campus as an enrolled ASU student. Once you complete a course and purchase the credits, it can take up to 14 business days for the course to appear on your unofficial ASU transcript. Learn more about requesting an ASU transcript 【17†here†students.asu.edu】.
L118: 
L119: How long do I have to add a course to my transcript?
L120: You have one year from the date you complete your course to purchase credit. You can see the exact date on your learner dashboard next to the course button that says “Add to transcript.”
L121: 
L122: I’m not happy with the grade I earned in my course. Can I take it again?
L123: Yes! You may enroll in the course the next time it is offered. However, on-demand courses cannot be reset. You may take the course the next time it is offered in a session-based format or wait until a new version of the on-demand course opens on July 1, the beginning of ASU’s fiscal year.
L124: 
L125: How can I tell if I already have credit from another institution?
L126: You can use the course search function of the 【18†Transfer Credit Guide†webapp4.asu.edu】 to find the course you took to determine if and how it might apply.
L127: 
L128: Can I take a Universal Learner Course to replace a grade from another institution?
L129: 
L130: No. If you have already completed a course, taking the same course with ULC will not replace the grade you earned at another institution.
L131: 
L132: How do my previous Universal Learner Courses align with the new ASU Gold Credit Designations?
L133: All ULCs that had a Maroon credit designation also have a Gold credit designation. That means courses you have taken previously with ULC will still apply to ASU major maps. Courses can fulfill requirements in both General Studies Gold and General Studies Maroon. Incoming ASU students will be required to meet the 【19†General Studies Gold requirements†catalog.asu.edu】. More information about these changes can be found on the 【20†Provost general studies page†provost.asu.edu】.
L134: How soon can I get credit for an on-demand course?
L135: 
L136: 3 and 4 credit on-demand courses will become available to add to your transcript 6 weeks after enrollment. 2 credit courses can be added after 4 weeks and a 1 credit course can be added after 2 weeks.
L137: 
L138: During which session will an on-demand course appear on my transcript?
L139: An on-demand course will appear on your transcript in the session in which you complete the course. Course attendance dates will also be listed on your transcript. If your completion date falls near the end of a session, please contact our support team at 【21†[email protected]】 at least three weeks before the session ends and before adding the course to your transcript to confirm which session it will fall under. Once the course has been added to your transcript, the session cannot be changed.
L140: Can Universal Learner Courses count toward NCAA eligibility?
L141: 
L142: High school students interested in using ASU Universal Learner Courses to meet NCAA core-course requirements should consult with their high school counselor or registrar. The high school is responsible for determining whether a Universal Learner Course can be categorized as dual enrollment, included in their curriculum, and reported to the NCAA as part of the student’s academic record.
L143: 
L144: 【22†Image: Graduation cap graphic】
L145: ## Degree programs
L146: 
L147: What is Earned Admission?
L148: Earned Admission provides a path for people at every stage of their career to earn a degree from Arizona State University. Anyone not currently enrolled at ASU can participate in Earned Admission by taking Universal Learner Courses. If you want to work towards a degree at ASU and aren’t ready to fully commit to university due to financial or scheduling reasons, Earned Admission is for you. To learn more about Earned Admission, please visit 【23†ea.asu.edu†ea.asu.edu】.
L149: Do I need a high school diploma or GED to earn admission into Arizona State University?
L150: 
L151: Yes, you need a high school diploma, GED or Affidavit of Completion of Secondary School Education to earn admission into ASU. This is part of the materials required on the ASU application. You can see all of the materials required 【5†here†asuonline.asu.edu】.
L152: 
L153: Can I use CLEP, AP, DANTES, or other national tests towards my Earned Admission requirements?
L154: No. However, national tests may be used for college credit once you are admitted to the university. Learn more about how your test credits may transfer 【24†here†catalog.asu.edu】.
L155: 
L156: What is a Degree Pathway?
L157: A low‑risk way to start ASU‑aligned courses in an interest area before formal admission. Degree Pathways allows a learner to select a degree program they are interested in and guides them on which ULCs will fit into that degree’s curriculum guide. Complete the pathway, then transition into your ASU degree.
L158: 
L159: What is the difference between Degree Pathways and Earned Admission?
L160: Degree Pathways is a way to guide your Earned Admission experience. All the same EA rules apply- you must complete 12 or 24 credits (depending on age) with a 2.75 GPA. However, some engineering programs have additional requirements like getting a 3.0 GPA or having a cumulative 3.0 GPA.
L161: 
L162: Does selecting a Degree Pathway mean I’m already enrolled in that degree program at ASU?
L163: No, Degree Pathways are designed to help track your progress toward a degree. You still have to apply to the university and select your desired program at ASU.
L164: 
L165: Does selecting an Engineering Pathway mean I’m automatically admitted to that program?
L166: No. Some Engineering Pathways have higher admission requirements, like having certain math or science competencies and a cumulative GPA of 3.0. Your cumulative GPA includes all previously transcripted course work from other institutions. If you have additional questions regarding a higher admission requirement Engineering Pathway, please contact our support team at 【11†[email protected]】.
L167: 
L168: What if I’m uncertain about what degree to pursue?
L169: If you’re currently unsure of your degree of interest, ASU offers the 【25†me3 career exploration tool†yourfuture.asu.edu】 to help you discover degree programs you may be interested in.
L170: 
L171: 【13†Image: Medal graphic】
L172: ## Certificates
L173: 
L174: How do I get started?
L175: 
L176: It’s easy! Begin completing the courses listed on the specific certificate page. Many certificate courses offer an on-demand option so you may begin at any time. Once you successfully complete and purchase all the courses required for a given certificate, you will receive an email containing your certificate with the ASU logo, your name and the name of the certificate you completed, along with transferable college credits.
L177: How long does it take to earn an ASU certificate?
L178: 
L179: Certificates consist of 3-6 courses, and learners typically take 1-2 classes at a time. The average completion time of each course is 8 weeks.
L180: 
L181: How do these courses appear on my transcript?
L182: 
L183: These courses appear identically to a course you would take online or on campus as an enrolled ASU student. Learn more about requesting a transcript 【26†here†registrar.asu.edu】.
L184: 
L185: Is there a minimum GPA requirement for earning an ASU Certificate?
L186: No, there is no minimum GPA requirement for certificates. However, If you’re using these courses to earn admission to ASU, you must pass each course with a C or better and have at least a 2.75 GPA to earn a certificate.
L187: 
L188: What happens if I enroll but don’t finish the requirements?
L189: While we hope everyone who enrolls will complete their certificate, there are no negative repercussions if you cannot finish the courses. ULC offers the opportunity to try college courses with low cost and low risk. Keep in mind, if you are having challenges with the coursework, tutoring is available to ensure you successfully complete the program. Visit the 【8†ULC Online Study Hub†tutoring.asu.edu】 for academic support.
L190: 
L191: Do I need to purchase all courses in the certificate to receive an ASU Certificate?
L192: Yes, to receive an ASU Certificate, you must add all of the courses to your transcript by purchasing the credits before receiving the credential. However, you have up to one year after completing each course to pay the credit fee.
L193: 
L194: Do ASU Certificate courses go towards admission into ASU if I take them while attending high school?
L195: No, the courses will not count toward Earned Admission for high school students. However, it is a great way to get a credential that you can put on your resume while on your way to pursuing a bachelor’s degree.
L196: 
L197: Can I use my corporate partner benefits for ASU Certificate courses?
L198: 
L199: Before enrolling in ASU’s Certificate programs, we recommend you check with your employer to confirm participation. Most corporate partners will not cover the cost of courses beyond what you need to be admitted.
L200: 【3†Image: Paper plane graphic】
L201: ## International learners
L202: 
L203: Can international learners take these courses?
L204: 
L205: Yes, with a few exceptions: learners cannot be located in a country that has restrictions of applicable embargoes and sanctions issued by the U.S. government. Learners hoping to use Universal Learner Courses for ASU admission would need to complete the 【27†application†asuonline.asu.edu】 for international students.
L206: 
L207: What are the English language requirements?
L208: Universal Learner Courses can be taken without proof of English proficiency. If you’re interested in applying for a degree and English is not your first language, ASU requires proof of English language proficiency. Check accepted English language tests 【28†here†admission.asu.edu】.
L209: 
L210: Do international students pay taxes?
L211: International students who do not enter the U.S. to complete their studies are not required to pay federal taxes for their education. ASU Online students living outside the U.S. aren’t able to obtain a visa to travel for the purpose of school. Those who don’t possess a U.S. visa for other purposes will select the option “JN-No-120 issued by ASU” in their applications.
L212: 
L213: 【29†Image: Computer graphic】
L214: ## Technical support
L215: 
L216: What laptop/setup do I need to take these courses?
L217: 
L218: Learn more about our technical requirements 【30†here】.
L219: 
L220: I just registered and I can’t log into my dashboard. Help!
L221: First, we suggest making sure this is not related to the ASURITE syncing timeline. As a refresher, it takes 2-3 business days to receive your ASURITE. Then it takes 24 hours to activate your ASURITE. Then, after that 24 hour period, you can use your ASURITE to login.
L222: If after this time period, you’re still having issues, please do reach out at 【11†[email protected]】.
L223: 
L224: What is two-factor authentication?
L225: Two-factor authentication protects you and your data by using a combination of your password (something you know) and a device that you own (like a phone) to access ASU systems. This is required for both login and exams. Learn more about Duo two-factor authentication 【31†here†docs.google.com】.
L226: 
L227: Can I access my Universal Learner Courses through the ASU Canvas App?

L4: # Proctoring
L5: 
L6: Ensuring that your course meets ASU’s academic and accreditation requirements for credit-bearing college courses.
L7: 
L8: 【2†Image: Student with laptop】
L9: ## What is proctoring?
L10: 
L11: Proctoring is the supervision of an exam or assignment to ensure integrity and prevent cheating. In Universal Learner Courses proctoring is delivered by additional software inside of the course experience that monitors your webcam and screen during specific assignments like quizzes and exams.
L12: 
L13: ## Why do some courses have proctored exams or quizzes?
L14: #### To ensure fairness and academic integrity.
L15: 
L16: Proctored exams confirm that all learners complete their own work under the same conditions, helping maintain fairness and uphold ASU’s academic standards. This protects the credibility of the credit you earn and ensures every learner’s grade reflects their own effort and understanding.
L17: #### To meet university and accreditation standards.
L18: 
L19: Some subjects (especially in math, sciences, and business) require verified assessment of learning outcomes. Proctoring ensures that the course meets ASU’s academic and accreditation requirements for credit-bearing college courses.
L20: #### To support transferability and credit recognition.
L21: 
L22:  Verified assessments help ensure that the credit you earn is recognized by ASU and, in many cases, by other institutions — because it meets the same standards as a regular ASU course.
L23: 
L24: #### Which courses have proctoring?
L25: 
L26: Use the “proctoring” filter in the course catalog to see Universal Learner Courses that require proctoring for assessment.
L27: ## System requirements
L28: 
L29: To ensure the software works on your computer, please meet the minimum system requirements outlined below.
L30:

L52: ## How does proctoring work?
L53: As you complete your exam or assignment with Honorlock, your computer’s screen and webcam will be monitored and recorded by a live Honorlock proctor. If you are flagged by the system or a proctor, the live virtual proctor will pop in to assess the situation, make sure there isn’t an academic violation, and help you get back on track with your exam.
L54: Honorlock also leverages an integrity algorithm that can detect search-engine use, so it’s important to not search for answers outside of the exam environment, even if it’s on a secondary device, like your cell phone or tablet.
L55: 【9†Image: ASU ULC website in laptop】
L56: 
L57: Honorlock testing policies are determined by the instructor and communicated in the syllabus. If the instructor does not set any specific policies, then the following are standard. Adhering to the following will ensure that you do not violate the online exam rules.
L58: #### Behavior:
L59: 
L60:   * Do not leave the exam environment at any time during the exam, unless specifically allowed in the exam instructions by your instructor
L61:   * Dress as if you were in a classroom setting
L62:   * Hats, hoods, headphones, earbuds, or earplugs are NOT allowed during the exam taking process
L63:   * Do not talk or communicate by any other means during the exam
L64: #### Environment:
L65:   * The environment must be quiet and fully lit
L66:   * You must be seated at a clean desk or table
L67:   * The exam must be taken in the same room that is scanned during the room scan
L68:   * The desk or table must be cleared of all materials not required for the exam unless specifically allowed in exam instructions
L69:   * Internet-capable devices such as a cell phone, e-reader, smartwatch, or internet-cable calculator must not be visible on the desk, table or testing area
L70:   * The camera must be focused on the test taker at all times
L71:   * No one other than the test-taker is permitted to enter the testing area during the exam
L72: Upon completion of the exam, once you click Submit Quiz, Honorlock will close and you will no longer be recorded or monitored.
L73: #### How is proctoring reviewed?
L74: 
L75: ####
L76: 
L77: Honorlock proctoring events are reviewed by the course team, and violations of proctoring policy may impact your score or eligibility to get credit in the course. If your instructional team has questions about footage of your proctoring event, they may contact you for more information.
L78: 
L79: #### Can I opt-out of proctoring?
L80: ####
L81: 
L82: No. There is no exclusion from proctoring requirements and if you do not want to download Honorlock software or participate in proctoring, you should refer to the ULC catalog for other courses that do not require proctoring.
